Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 6 Jul 2026 15:23:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood trial — procurement & billing next steps

Hi Sam —

Great to meet you and Priya today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

1) Trial scope & success criteria
- Goal: validate Redwood inference for customer-facing summarization workflows across 3 teams.
- Success criteria: sustained inference throughput for 5 concurrent streams, <150ms P95 latency, and evaluation pass on the sample prompt set (~90% of prompts returning acceptable outputs).

2) Procurement & commercial path
- You mentioned procurement prefers PO for any production spend. For the trial we can accept card, but if you want to convert to paid with a PO we can route through our finance team.
- Marketplace: Redwood is listed on AWS Marketplace; if Acme prefers that route it will simplify billing and the PO can reference the marketplace subscription. That typically adds ~1 week to setup on top of the procurement approval.

3) Administrative artifacts (attached)
- SOW-draft.pdf (high-level trial scope & indicative pricing)
- procurement-checklist.xlsx (fields your procurement team usually asks for)

Proposed practical timeline:
- Run trial through July 20, 2026.
- If success criteria met, convert to paid beginning July 21, 2026 (start of billing month) unless you prefer to align to a PO effective date.

Can you confirm: 1) procurement path (PO vs card vs Marketplace), 2) if July 21 works as billing start, and 3) any specific PO template to attach to the SOW?

I copied Dylan (solutions) to help with any technical gating and to coordinate the billing toggle when you’re ready. I can also start a DocuSign if you want the SOW signed now to lock scope.

Thanks —
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
(415) 555-0123

From: Sam Torres <sam.torres@acme.com>

Date: Tue, 7 Jul 2026 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood trial — procurement & billing next steps

Thanks Marissa — good recap. A few follow-ups from procurement on our side: 

- PO vs card: Acme procurement prefers PO for anything that could become production. For a short pilot we sometimes allow a corporate card, but given potential scale we’d like to get the PO route started so there’s no delay on conversion.
- Marketplace: we'd prefer AWS Marketplace if possible as it fits our internal chargeback model, but we need to confirm that your pricing matches the SOW when sold via marketplace. Does Redwood support marketplace subscriptions that align 1:1 with the SOW line items?
- Security docs: procurement requested a copy of your SOC2 and an export of the trial data retention policy. Who should they contact for those artifacts?

Also, I attached our PO template (acme-po-template.docx) — please confirm whether Redwood requires any edits.

If we can align on PO + marketplace options, we can start the procurement approval this week.

—Sam
Sam Torres
Head of Procurement — Acme Corp
sam.torres@acme.com

Attachment: acme-po-template.docx

Sam — thanks, that's helpful. Quick answers inline:

- PO vs card: We can absolutely accept a PO for the trial-to-paid conversion. For the hosted API (self-serve) many teams use card during evaluation because it’s faster, but since you expect production scale and want PO we’ll coordinate Finance to allow PO billing once the trial converts. Will need your PO number and billing contact to create the invoice.

- Marketplace: Yes — Redwood supports AWS Marketplace subscriptions. Pricing on the marketplace is usually equivalent but sometimes needs a simple mapping between our list/usage line items and the marketplace SKU. Dev, can you confirm the mapping steps?

- Security artifacts: Our security team can share SOC 2 Type II and the trial data retention policy. I'll introduce Melissa from Security if you want direct docs and an SSA (security self-assessment).

Proposed approach:
1) You submit PO for the estimated monthly commit (or say "TBD" and we invoice after conversion) — attach PO template.
2) We sign the SOW (DocuSign link below) to lock scope.
3) Trial runs through July 20; if success criteria are met we flip billing to the PO/subscription with effective date July 21.

DocuSign (SOW): https://www.docusign.net/Member/PowerFormSigning.aspx?env=na1&acct=12345678
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/company/987654

If that works, I’ll loop in Finance to provision the invoice flow and Melissa on security.

Thanks —
Marissa

Hi team — quick technical and process notes from my side: 

- Marketplace mapping: We have a standard SKU mapping doc for AWS Marketplace that aligns with our SOW line items (tokens, dedicated capacity, support). I can share the mapping and confirm equivalence to the SOW. Typically the work to map the SKU and set up billing on Marketplace is 3–7 business days.

- Billing start trigger: We recommend starting invoicing on the first day after the trial success criteria are met. For clarity we can set a usage threshold (e.g., more than 1M prompt tokens or sustained 5 concurrent streams for 48 hours) as the "conversion trigger." Once the trigger is reached, we flip billing to the PO/subscription and backdate the invoice to the agreed effective date (e.g., July 21).

- PO template: I reviewed the attached acme-po-template.docx — a couple of minor billing contact fields need Redwood's billing email (billing@redwood.com) and our tax info; Finance will send a redlined version if that’s acceptable.

I’m happy to run a short call with your procurement/security folks to walk the mapping and timeline.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
